register: Formal political and institutional verb for overturning an established order or corrupting an organization’s operation from within.
trap: Subvertir suggests a fundamental alteration of an established order; saper in item 222 instead emphasizes gradual weakening, while renverser denotes outright overthrow.
example_tl: Des réseaux clandestins cherchaient à subvertir l’ordre constitutionnel en infiltrant les syndicats, les médias et les administrations encore fragilisées par la guerre.
example_en: Clandestine networks sought to subvert the constitutional order by infiltrating trade unions, media outlets, and government departments still weakened by the war.
cloze: Des réseaux clandestins cherchaient à {{c1::subvertir}} l’ordre constitutionnel en infiltrant les syndicats, les médias et les administrations encore fragilisées par la guerre.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained this formal verb because its direct alteration of an established order contrasts materially with the gradual erosion expressed by saper in item 222.

register: Neutral environmental and land-use verb for removing forest cover from an area; déforester is a more technical alternative, especially for large-scale forest loss.
trap: Défricher adds the idea of clearing land for cultivation or development and is therefore not interchangeable with déboiser in every context.
example_tl: Le régime a déboisé de vastes zones frontalières pour ouvrir des routes militaires, accélérant l’érosion et le déplacement de communautés rurales.
example_en: The regime deforested vast border areas to open military roads, accelerating erosion and the displacement of rural communities.
cloze: Le régime a {{c1::déboisé}} de vastes zones frontalières pour ouvrir des routes militaires, accélérant l’érosion et le déplacement de communautés rurales.
note: Old_back supplies the idiomatic neutral verb. Self-review retained déforester only as a contextually interchangeable technical alternative and separated both terms from the purpose-specific défricher.

register: Neutral media verb for broadcasting content to an audience; émettre is equally natural here but foregrounds the station’s transmission activity.
trap: Retransmettre normally means to relay or rebroadcast a signal, program, or event and should not replace the generic English broadcast automatically.
example_tl: Pendant la crise, la station clandestine diffusait chaque soir des bulletins codés afin de coordonner l’opposition et de contourner la censure officielle.
example_en: During the crisis, the clandestine station broadcast coded bulletins every evening to coordinate the opposition and circumvent official censorship.
cloze: Pendant la crise, la station clandestine {{c1::diffusait}} chaque soir des bulletins codés afin de coordonner l’opposition et de contourner la censure officielle.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review kept émettre because it fits the same radio-station example and excluded retransmettre, which would imply relaying an event or another source’s signal.

register: Neutral-formal verb, commonly used absolutely or with dans or en matière de to specify the field in which innovation occurs.
trap: In careful French, innover is normally intransitive: one innove dans un domaine rather than mechanically calquing English innovate a technology with a direct object.
example_tl: Pour réduire sa dépendance technologique, le programme spatial devait innover dans les télécommunications sans importer de composants soumis aux contrôles occidentaux.
example_en: To reduce its technological dependence, the space program had to innovate in telecommunications without importing components subject to Western controls.
cloze: Pour réduire sa dépendance technologique, le programme spatial devait {{c1::innover}} dans les télécommunications sans importer de composants soumis aux contrôles occidentaux.
note: Old_back gives the correct lemma but not its construction. Self-review retained the item for its consequential intransitive pattern and avoided claiming that every contemporary transitive use is impossible.

register: Neutral-formal and highly productive in political prose for sanctions, restrictions, conditions, obligations, and financial burdens.
trap: English impose sanctions on a country maps to imposer des sanctions à un pays; sur cannot mechanically replace à before the affected recipient.
example_tl: Après l’essai nucléaire, plusieurs gouvernements ont imposé de nouvelles restrictions commerciales au régime, malgré les réserves de leurs secteurs industriels les plus exposés.
example_en: After the nuclear test, several governments imposed new trade restrictions on the regime, despite reservations from their most exposed industrial sectors.
cloze: Après l’essai nucléaire, plusieurs gouvernements ont {{c1::imposé}} de nouvelles restrictions commerciales {{c1::au}} régime, malgré les réserves de leurs secteurs industriels les plus exposés.
note: Old_back supplies only the verb. Self-review retained the broader political frame beyond the earlier embargo expression and clozed the inflected verb and recipient preposition separately.

register: Neutral-formal verb for responding forcefully to an attack, sanction, or hostile act; common in diplomatic and military reporting.
trap: French riposte à an act or measure; retaliation against an actor may instead require exercer des représailles contre, while se venger de sounds more personal.
example_tl: Le gouvernement a riposté aux sanctions économiques en expulsant deux diplomates, tout en évitant les mesures militaires susceptibles d’élargir la crise.
example_en: The government retaliated against the economic sanctions by expelling two diplomats while avoiding military measures liable to widen the crisis.
cloze: Le gouvernement {{c1::a riposté aux}} sanctions économiques en expulsant deux diplomates, tout en évitant les mesures militaires susceptibles d’élargir la crise.
note: Materially improves old_back ('pour riposter'), which includes a purpose marker rather than a production-ready headword. Self-review selected the trigger construction riposter à and kept actor-directed reprisals as a contrast.

register: Formal argumentative expression for publicly supporting a policy or course of action; préconiser recommends it, while défendre foregrounds active support.
trap: Plaider requires pour in this sense, whereas préconiser and défendre take a direct object; carrying pour over to either alternative produces the wrong construction.
example_tl: Plusieurs diplomates ont plaidé pour une levée progressive des sanctions, conditionnée à des inspections indépendantes et au démantèlement vérifiable des installations secrètes.
example_en: Several diplomats advocated a gradual lifting of sanctions, conditional on independent inspections and the verifiable dismantling of secret facilities.
cloze: Plusieurs diplomates {{c1::ont plaidé pour}} une levée progressive des sanctions, conditionnée à des inspections indépendantes et au démantèlement vérifiable des installations secrètes.
note: Materially refines old_back ('préconiser'): that verb fits the policy example, but plaider pour better teaches the advocacy frame. Self-review verified both direct-object alternatives in the same sentence after normal inflection.

register: Neutral-formal support-verb expression for deliberately formulating a plan; the alternative emphasizes refining it until it is operational.
trap: English strategize normally becomes a support-verb expression in careful French; agir stratégiquement means to act strategically, not to formulate a strategy.
example_tl: Avant le sommet, les conseillers ont élaboré une stratégie commune pour exploiter les divisions adverses sans compromettre la reprise des négociations.
example_en: Before the summit, the advisers devised a common strategy to exploit divisions among their adversaries without jeopardizing the resumption of negotiations.
cloze: Avant le sommet, les conseillers {{c1::ont élaboré une stratégie}} commune pour exploiter les divisions adverses sans compromettre la reprise des négociations.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review retained the support-verb treatment, verified that the alternative fits before commune, and distinguished planning from merely acting in a strategic manner.

register: Saper and miner are formal figurative verbs suggesting progressive erosion; affaiblir is neutral and states the weakening without that metaphorical nuance.
trap: Saper does not always equal subvertir: undermine often weakens trust or capacity gradually, whereas subvertir in item 202 alters an established order more directly.
example_tl: Des campagnes de désinformation ont sapé la confiance dans les institutions électorales, transformant chaque défaite en preuve supposée d’une ingérence étrangère.
example_en: Disinformation campaigns undermined trust in electoral institutions, turning every defeat into supposed evidence of foreign interference.
cloze: Des campagnes de désinformation ont {{c1::sapé}} la confiance dans les institutions électorales, transformant chaque défaite en preuve supposée d’une ingérence étrangère.
note: Old_back is accurate. Self-review removed subvertir as an alternative because item 202 tests a distinct sense and verified that miner and affaiblir both fit the example after inflection.
